doc.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

chapter: Jaco, Weather Report and pop work
title: Playing drums in Blood, Sweat & Tears
summary: He moved from percussion to the drum chair after Bobby Colomby left, played for salary near the end of their success, and chats with Rowe about the band today.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh yeah he was back in then, back in the days. And of course Blood, Sweat & Tears. That was a wonderful experience because I started playing percussion and then moved over to the drum set. Bobby Columby, who had been doing it from the beginning, decided that he wanted to stay home I guess and collect the money. And I moved over to the drum chair, and for me that was a great challenge. Again, here comes the challenge. And the writers in the band were great, Larry Willis, Tony Klatka, they were great writers, they would write material for the band, jazz orientated but you know it had that © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -18-

Blood, Sweat and Tears sound. So they also, if you consider them a Pop group, because they were very successful. I came in at the very tail end of the success you know. I was on salary. I didn’t share in any of the revenues, shall we say, in the band.
David Clayton Thomas was gone at that time, wasn’t he?
He had come back. When I came back in the band he had come back. He was a great singer for that type of stuff.
Yes I have. One of my high school buddies is now like the music director, it’s interesting.
Steve Guttman. A trumpet player. Interesting. They sound good. They sound very close to the recordings. That’s what they’re about.
